title: Fulbright Iceland-National Science Foundation Arctic Research Grants
description: A research grant placing post-master's and PhD-level US researchers in Iceland for up to 9 months to conduct NSF-funded Arctic-relevant research, through a partnership between the Fulbright Program and the U.S. National Science Foundation. Eligible fields include glaciology, geology, biology, sustainability science, and other natural or social science fields relevant to Arctic research. Post-master's grantees receive USD 2,100/month; PhD students/candidates receive USD 2,750/month plus an additional USD 300/month research stipend, both for up to 9 months, intended to cover housing, meals, and incidental costs. Grant benefits also include a travel stipend and baggage allowance to Iceland, supplemental accident and sickness coverage, and access to Fulbright Iceland enrichment activities. Open to US citizens holding at least a bachelor's degree who have completed a master's degree or are PhD students/candidates; applicants who already reside in Iceland or are Icelandic permanent residents are not eligible. This entry covers the 2027-2028 grant cycle (grants begin no earlier than mid-August 2027).
org: U.S. Department of State (Fulbright Program) / National Science Foundation / Fulbright Iceland
visaNote: This is a Fulbright research grant, not employment; visa/residence permit arrangements for Iceland are coordinated as part of the Fulbright grant.
